_README: TEMPLATE, not live data. Copy to the box as /data/mpc-candidates.json (or point
MPC_CANDIDATE_BANK at it) and replace every record with people you actually represent.
Validate with: node tools/mpc-bank.mjs --check --bank <path>
Four fields do the work:
proof   Exactly two facts, and they must be a PAIRING, not a duty list. Two things
that are ordinary alone and hard to find in one person. 'Owned month-end
close' proves nothing because every applicant says it. 'Took a manual close
to five days' plus 'ran the ERP migration underneath it' is a person.
pitchFor  Optional. Titles this person should answer, matched as substrings of the open
role. Without it a record only answers reqs whose title shares a real word with
its own, so a Controller is never pitched as a Junior Accountant. Use pitchFor
to widen that on purpose.
reason  Why someone this good is available. This is the sentence that turns a claim
into a human being, and it is the one thing no model can infer. Without it
the email falls back to 'they're looking quietly', which persuades nobody.
metro   Where they are. Omit for a person open anywhere, or set remoteOk true.
family  Optional. Inferred from the title when absent. Must match the open role's
family for the record to be used, so a Controller is never pitched into a
sales req.
Numbers are allowed ONLY here. Anything in a proof line goes into the email verbatim,
and the render gate blocks every quantity the writer produces on its own. So a number
in a sent email is always a number you typed.

candidates.title: Controller
proof: Took a manual close down to five days
Ran the ERP migration underneath it
candidates.reason: Their CFO seat went to an outside hire

candidates.title: VP of Sales
proof: Built the enterprise team from two reps
Carried a number themselves the whole time
candidates.reason: Their company pivoted to product-led and cut the enterprise motion

candidates.title: FP&A Manager
proof: Owns the model and the board deck
Came up through accounting, so the numbers tie
candidates.reason: Their CFO left and the new one brought their own bench
